ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, and directors against PEP databases, OFAC's SDN list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and the Spanish domestic AML/CFT risk indicators. Enhanced due diligence is applied automatically to persons connected to high-risk third countries, tax-haven-listed jurisdictions, or countries subject to FATF call for action; all screening results must be documented and retained for at least 10 years as required by Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Ministerio de Justicia (telematic name reservation service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in Spanish or any official language of the European Union; foreign-language names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The corporate form suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' must be included. The name must not be identical to an existing Spanish or EU-registered company, must not infringe protected trademarks, and must not be contrary to public order or misleading as to the corporate form or activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The certificación negativa de denominación social is valid for 90 days from issuance. If the application is rejected, submit a new application listing at least 3 alternative names. An administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be filed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of formal notification. There is no extension of the 90-day reservation; if incorporation documents are not presented to the Mercantile Registry before expiry, a fresh clearance certificate must be obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual/registered-agent office is initially permissible for correspondence and registration purposes, but a PO Box alone is not accepted. For wholesale trade of copper cathodes, Spanish banking AML compliance, documentary LC against LME warrants, and VAT obligations require demonstrable operational substance: a physical or shared premises in Spain, local management, and document-keeping capacity. A purely virtual office is therefore acceptable only during pre-incorporation and the first months of activity; the supervisor may require a physical presence for full commercial compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate likelihood, estimated at 15-20% during the first year of operations. Spanish tax authorities and AML/CFT audit institutions may carry out unannounced on-site inspections to verify economic substance, particularly for a metals trading entity with medium-risk AML classification; incorporating with a compliant registered office and record-keeping reduces this risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-23, 28-30, 62, 78-80, 159-210, and 210-242; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, under the coordination of the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, filed for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve and, upon liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders have joint and several liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. Capital must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. A separate bank escrow account is not mandatory where the deed contains the founders' express statement accepting liability for the existence and payment of the contributions; otherwise, a bank certificate of deposit is generally provided.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription and full payment of its issued quotas by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted and entered in the corporate records; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, where applicable, [names] are appointed joint or several directors, each accepting office and declaring no statutory incompatibility; (4) the appointed officer is authorised to obtain the tax identification number, register the deed, open bank accounts, and complete all ancillary governmental filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service or an authorised filing agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identifying the preferred name and the proposed SL legal form. Obtain the negative certificate of company name. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for registration reservation purposes. Foreign corporate shareholders should provide legalized and apostilled constitutional documents and a current good-standing certificate, with sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: Identification of proposed shareholder or shareholders
Powers of attorney for filing agent, if applicable
Legalized or apostilled foreign shareholder documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name. If the certificate expires before execution, obtain a new certificate. Any registry query must be answered through the filing agent or registry presentation channel within the stated cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles and Notarial Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary Public (notario público) selected by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, identify the shareholder and beneficial owner, define the corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, quota allocation, governance model, and director appointment. Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary. Foreign individuals generally require a Spanish foreigner identification number (NIE); foreign entities require a Spanish tax identification number and legalized corporate authority documents.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identification and NIE or tax identification number
Foreign corporate documents, apostilled or legalized and translated where required
Evidence of capital payment or founders' statutory payment-liability statement
Power of attorney, if signing through an attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting defects identified by the notary and re-execute or supplement the deed. Replace defective powers, translations, or legalization certificates before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification and Register with the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) and the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the AEAT for the provisional NIF using Form 036, then submit the electronically transmitted or paper public deed to the Provincial Mercantile Registry. Pay the applicable variable notarial, registry, publication, and filing charges. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update the AEAT registration data.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of applicable registry charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry qualification notice by correcting the deed, filing supplemental documents, or appealing under the Mercantile Registry Regulations. Re-present the cured filing within the applicable validity period and obtain a renewed tax certificate if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Corporate Books and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry through its electronic corporate-books filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize the shareholders' register, minutes book, and other mandatory corporate books electronically within the statutory period following the financial year-end. Record the first board or sole-director resolutions, director acceptance, beneficial ownership information, powers of attorney, and quota transfers. Maintain accounting records and prepare annual accounts in accordance with Spanish accounting law.
required_dossiers: Powers of attorney and corporate signature authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic books or incomplete records and resubmit through the Mercantile Registry platform. Rectify governance defects through a supplemental resolution or notarized deed where legally required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Commercial Activity and Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal town-planning and economic-activity authority (Ayuntamiento) and, where applicable, the competent autonomous-community industrial or environmental authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before operating a warehouse or commercial premises, verify zoning compatibility and submit the applicable responsible declaration, prior communication, opening notice, or municipal activity licence. For copper cathode storage, document site layout, storage loads, fire protection, access, waste procedures, and occupational-risk controls. Obtain any environmental or hazardous-material authorisations triggered by the actual premises, quantities, processes, or transport activities.
required_dossiers: Environmental and waste-management documentation, if applicable
Civil liability and property insurance evidence, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer municipal or regional technical objections, amend the technical project, obtain missing certificates, and resubmit the responsible declaration or licence application. Do not commence regulated physical operations until the applicable prior-control requirements are satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial authority of the autonomous community in which the premises are located, together with the relevant municipality. Pure wholesale trading of refined copper cathodes generally has no sector-specific national manufacturing licence; warehousing and premises operation may require municipal prior control and activity authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal declaration of responsibility or prior communication for commencement of commercial or warehouse activity (declaración responsable or comunicación previa de inicio de actividad), or municipal activity licence where required by the applicable autonomous-community and local rules. No manufacturing permit is ordinarily required unless the company performs processing, treatment, or industrial transformation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and the applicable autonomous-community environmental legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from EIA for ordinary wholesale and storage of solid copper cathodes without processing, combustion, significant emissions, or hazardous-waste treatment. A screening or full assessment may arise if the facility, project scale, location, or associated infrastructure falls within Annex I or Annex II of Law 21/2013 or regional legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific copper-cathode process-emission threshold ordinarily applies to an unprocessed storage and trading operation. The operator must prevent soil and water contamination, manage any waste under Law 7/2022 on Waste and Contaminated Soils, obtain a discharge authorization for any regulated water discharge, comply with applicable air-quality and industrial-emissions rules, and use authorised waste managers. Storage of oils, chemicals, packaging waste, or contaminated materials may trigger additional hazardous-substance and waste obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must satisfy the Spanish fire-safety framework, including Royal Decree 2267/2004 for industrial establishments where applicable, the Building Code fire provisions, and municipal fire-service requirements. Obtain technical fire-protection certificates, emergency and evacuation plans, and any required inspection certificates. Verify floor loading, racks, lifting equipment, and structural integrity through a competent technician. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, worker training, personal protective equipment, handling procedures, contractor controls, and emergency arrangements. Dangerous-goods transport or storage, if applicable, requires additional ADR and regional hazardous-installation compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — the Spanish Tax Administration Agency — is the sole competent authority for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax), IVA (VAT) and customs in mainland Spain. Electronic filing is effected through the Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) and the AEAT Customs SGL system; the local AEAT Delegación/Administración corresponding to the SL's fiscal domicile handles census, SII compliance and tax audits. The Basque Country and Navarre maintain separate foral tax regimes outside the AEAT scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary and obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via Modelo 036 presented at the AEAT. Step 2: Register the SL in the Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry). Step 3: File the definitive Modelo 036 (declaración censal de alta) within one month of commencement to (i) obtain the definitive NIF, (ii) enroll in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders, (iii) elect the IVA filing regime (general, monthly, or SII if turnover exceeds EUR 6,010,121.24), and (iv) register as taxpayer of Impuesto sobre Sociedades and as a withholding agent (Modelos 123/216 for payments to non-residents). Step 4: Obtain an electronic signature certificate (certificado electrónico) from an AEAT-accredited issuer and the Cl@ve PIN for Sede Electrónica, SII web services and the customs SGL. Step 5: If foreign shareholders hold the SL, they must hold a NIF for non-residents (Modelo 030); the SL is the withholding agent on distributions. Step 6: Register in VIES through Modelo 036 for intra-community transactions and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a separate tax subject under art. 7 of Ley 27/2014 (LIS), taxed on worldwide income and gains (arts. 4 and 8 LIS); no pass-through or transparent attribution to shareholders arises under Spanish domestic law. The standard Corporate Income Tax rate is 25% (art. 29 LIS). A reduced 15% rate applies for the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base of a newly created entity conducting an economic activity, except where more than 50% of the capital belongs to non-residents from tax haven jurisdictions. The SL is not situated in a Tax_Exempt_Zone, and territorial restrictions do not apply to a Spanish resident entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Elections available under Spanish law: (i) consolidated tax group treatment for a parent holding directly or indirectly at least 75% of the SL (arts. 64-75 LIS); (ii) reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created entities (art. 29.1 LIS), exercised at each provisional payment; (iii) VAT group regime for 100%-controlled entities (art. 163 quaterdecies LIVA); (iv) OSS/Union one-stop-shop election for intra-EU distance sales (arts. 66-73 LIVA); (v) customs economic regimes (inward processing, customs warehousing, end-use) by AEAT authorization through SGL; (vi) transfer-pricing method selection for controlled metal-trading transactions (arts. 16 and 18 LIS); (vii) patent box election (art. 23 LIS) for qualifying intangibles, though not relevant to copper cathode trading. Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; hybrid mismatch adjustments under Directive (EU) 2016/1164 apply mandatorily rather than by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish VAT, harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC and Ley 37/1992 (LIVA). Mainland Spain applies IVA; the Canary Islands apply IGIC and Ceuta/Melilla apply IPSI, outside the mainland scope of this dossier. Imports and exports of copper cathodes are administered by AEAT Aduanas within the IVA framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — there is no turnover threshold for VAT registration of an established Spanish SL; art. 164 LIVA requires registration from the first economic activity regardless of volume. The only quantitative threshold relevant is EUR 6,010,121.24 of annual turnover, which triggers mandatory enrollment in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información). The EUR 10,000 Union-OSS threshold for intra-EU distance sales is not applicable to an established SL.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Two digitally distinct mandates apply cumulatively: (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) — compulsory for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,010,121.24, which is fully relevant to an active wholesale copper-trading SL. All issued invoices (including LME warrant sale invoices) and all received invoices must be transmitted to the AEAT SII web services (SOAP/XML, specification v2.x) within 4 calendar days of issue or receipt (8 days for monthly aggregated batches). The AEAT SII repository constitutes the legal VAT books. Spain does not operate a Latin-American-style real-time fiscal clearance with digital stamping. (2) Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 — all B2B invoices and credit notes must be issued in Facturae XML (or an interoperable equivalent) and submitted through a digital platform (private certified provider or the AEAT free portal); the platform must make the invoice data accessible to the AEAT. Application is phased between approximately end-2025 for taxpayers with revenue above EUR 8,000,000 and end-2026 for all other taxpayers. The electronic invoice data under (2) does not replace but may feed the SII submission under (1).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under art. 21 LIVA, exports of copper cathodes to destinations outside the EU customs territory are exempt with credit (0% IVA) provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch. For LME warrant trading, the transfer of a warrant is a supply of goods taxable at 21% if the metal remains in a Spanish or other EU LME warehouse; zero-rating applies only upon physical export outside the EU or upon intra-community supply to a VAT-registered counterparty in another Member State (art. 25 LIVA), subject to possession of the customer's valid NIF-VAT, the Modelo 349 recapitulative statement and dispatch evidence. Offshore services supplied to non-established recipients (art. 69 LIVA) and certain international freight services (art. 68 LIVA) may also qualify for zero-rating. The SL may deduct related input VAT on copper purchases, warehousing, commissions and customs clearing in the periodic Modelo 303; where deductible IVA exceeds output IVA, a refund arises in the same settlement, which is common in export-heavy operations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) lodged electronically via the AEAT Aduanas SGL system, generating the MRN evidencing exit from the EU; the declaration must state tariff classification HS 7403.11 and net mass of the Grade A copper cathodes

Bill of Lading (or CMR/AWB/multimodal transport document) evidencing physical dispatch from a Spanish or EU port to a destination outside the EU, with consistent vessel, date, weight and consignee data
Inward remittance certificate (bank/FX documentation, SWIFT MT103 or documentary LC settlement notice) evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in Spain within the commercial payment term
Commercial invoice and packing list bearing the SL's NIF, ISIC 4662 scope description, HS code, LME Grade A specification (Cu min 99.99%), parcel and net weight, and warrant references
LME warehouse warrant / delivery order and certificate of analysis corroborating the physical lot stored at the LME warehouse
Documentary Letter of Credit settlement file (MT700/MT754/MT760) together with the presentation set (draft, packing list, weight certificates, insurance documents) covering the payment rail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT inspection reconciles the DUA/MRN against transport and banking evidence; any mismatch defeats the zero-rating and the supply is re-characterized as taxable at 21% IVA, with statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora). Sanctions under Law 58/2003 (LGT) range from 1% (leve) to 50%-100% (grave) and 100%-150% (muy grave) of the tax amount; incorrect or late SII records attract a fixed penalty of EUR 200 per record, with a minimum of EUR 400 and a maximum of EUR 20,000 per filing period. Fraudulent export zero-rating, including carousel or tornaviaje arrangements and knowing participation in a VAT evasion chain, triggers loss of input VAT deduction, joint and several liability, and criminal prosecution under art. 305 of the Criminal Code where defrauded IVA exceeds EUR 120,000 per year (imprisonment of 1-5 years and fines of up to six times the evaded amount). Retrospective clawback is generally limited to four years by prescription under art. 66 LGT, while criminal proceedings extend to ten years under art. 131 CP.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the Spanish supervisory authority for banking, balance-of-payments reporting and foreign-exchange market conduct within the Eurosystem/European System of Central Banks. Capital-movement and foreign-investment control functions are shared with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commerce and Enterprise, through the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) of the General Directorate for International Trade and Investment (DGCIIN). The European Central Bank holds exclusive monetary-policy authority for the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full euro-area member; the euro is freely convertible on both current and capital account. Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantee free movement of capital throughout the EU/EEA and vis-à-vis third countries, subject only to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax-transparency rules and the national foreign-investment screening regime of Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 571/2023. The ISIC 4662 copper-cathode wholesale activity is not listed as a critical sector; therefore no prior exchange-control authorization applies to export/import payments, capital injections or profit remittance. Nontheless, a non-resident shareholder's repatriation of dividends is subject to a 19% Spanish withholding tax (rate may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty), and a post-closing statistical declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry is required when a foreign investor acquires more than 10% of the SL and the transaction value equals or exceeds EUR 3,000,000 (or when a non-EU/EFTA investor acquires 10% or more of a Spanish entity active in defence, dual-use, critical energy, telecommunications, media, cybersecurity or other reserved sectors).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain export receipts in any freely convertible currency, in resident or non-resident accounts. For statistical and anti-money-laundering purposes, the receiving bank reports each export-related credit to the Banco de España under the 'Operaciones con el Exterior' (BC-2) balance-of-payments file and the exporter must be able to match the receipt against the underlying export contract, the Single Administrative Document (customs declaration) and Intrastat filings for intra-EU movements. There is no obligation to convert USD receipts into EUR; however, a company with EUR-denominated operating costs may reasonably contract an FX forward to hedge balance-sheet exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Capital) / Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) with multi-currency and trade-finance facility
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) / Documentary Letter of Credit and FX Hedging Desk
Operational Account (Cuenta de Operaciones) / Credit and Warrant Transfer Settlement Account
Operational Account / Documentary Collection and Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account / Electronic Banking and FX Platform

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 3,000 EUR and risk of dissolution proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if company exceeds two of: net turnover exceeding 4 million EUR, total assets exceeding 2 million EUR, or average employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (PGC - Plan General de Contabilidad)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership register must be maintained and updated upon any change; annual accounts filing provides periodic confirmation mechanism to Registro Mercantil

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate for Spanish-resident companies, including an SL. The rate may be reduced for qualifying entities under transitional or special rules; confirm eligibility and the applicable tax year before filing.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created entities generally apply a 15% rate in their first tax period with a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Other relief may include the patent-box regime, qualifying R&D and technological-innovation tax credits, and incentives for qualifying small entities. Certain micro and small entities have transitional reduced rates; eligibility and rates depend on turnover and tax year. No incentive applies solely because the business trades copper cathodes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite; Spain generally imposes no fixed expiry. Utilisation is subject to taxable-base limits, minimum utilisation rules, and statutory exceptions. The requested five-year limit does not reflect Spanish law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic office using an accepted electronic certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the accounting period closes. For a 31 December year-end, the ordinary filing window is 1–25 July, subject to the applicable calendar and electronic-filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish tax identification number, legal name, registered address, tax residence, accounting period, and applicable return type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish-incorporated SL is generally Spanish tax-resident and files as a resident company even if its shareholders are non-residents. Report non-resident shareholders accurately; do not treat the SL as a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the applicable corporate tax regime and report accounting profit or loss and relevant financial-statement information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary resident-company regime unless the SL meets requirements for a special regime. Shareholder residence does not itself change the SL's regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, tax depreciation differences, exempt income, related-party adjustments, and carried-forward tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Spain-source income and expenses of the resident SL under the resident-company rules. Retain evidence for deductions, loss utilisation, and arm's-length related-party pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, tax credits, and tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the legally applicable rate, claim eligible deductions and credits, and calculate the final corporate income tax liability after permitted offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply any reduced rate only if the SL satisfies the statutory conditions for the relevant tax period. Non-resident ownership alone does not qualify the SL for a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit qualifying advance payments and withholding tax against the annual liability and calculate the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Modelo 202 instalments and other Spanish tax credits to the SL's records; do not claim shareholder-level withholding as a company credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the applicable related-party, loss-carryforward, deduction, and other schedules required by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant cross-border related-party transactions and maintain documentation. A separate Modelo 232 may be required for reportable related-party transactions or specified transactions with related parties in tax havens.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late return filed voluntarily without prior assessment generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, with late-payment interest also due. Where the return is filed after a tax-authority request, or where a return is omitted, tax, interest, and tax-penalty rules may apply. Formal filing failures can also attract fixed penalties. Exact consequences depend on whether tax is payable, the filing circumstances, and any correction or reduction rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax instalment-payment form, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment dates; filing is generally required for companies subject to the instalment-payment obligation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ordinary filing and payment windows are 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December. The applicable statutory method determines the instalment calculation; qualifying companies may be subject to the taxable-base method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the SL, tax period, and relevant instalment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident Spanish SL files for itself. Its non-resident shareholders are not substituted as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory calculation method applicable to the company and report the relevant prior-year liability or current-period taxable-base information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's Spanish corporate tax data and applicable method. Do not calculate the instalment on a shareholder's foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply eligible prior instalments and credits and pay the resulting amount by the deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile payments to the SL's AEAT account and retain payment confirmations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may result in statutory surcharges and interest; failure to file or pay may also trigger tax-enforcement measures and penalties. The amount depends on the filing history, whether the taxpayer acts voluntarily or after an authority notice, and whether tax remains unpaid.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish domestic withholding on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions and reductions under Spanish law, EU law, and an applicable tax treaty. The rate and relief depend on the recipient, beneficial ownership, residence, and evidence provided.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, provide the Spanish payer with a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's competent tax authority and the documentation required to establish treaty entitlement, beneficial ownership, and any applicable limitation or anti-abuse conditions. The payer applies a reduced rate or exemption only where legally supported and retains the evidence. If withholding at the domestic rate has already occurred, the recipient may generally seek a refund from the AEAT using the applicable non-resident refund procedure and supporting residence and payment evidence. EU parent-subsidiary relief requires satisfaction of its statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions; a certificate of residence alone does not establish entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-resident withholding is generally 19% on interest and 24% on royalties paid to non-residents, subject to the recipient's status and applicable exemptions or treaty limits. A treaty may reduce these rates; the applicable Spain treaty must be checked for the specific recipient and income. Qualifying EU/EEA interest or royalty payments may be exempt under Spanish implementation of the Interest and Royalties Directive if all statutory conditions, including associated-company and beneficial-owner requirements, are met. Spanish-source character, permanent-establishment attribution, and domestic-law exceptions require case-specific review.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Related-party transactions must generally be valued at arm's length and documented. The principal documentation exemption threshold is generally €250,000 of transactions, measured at market value with the same related person during the tax period, subject to important exceptions. Additional exemptions and simplified-documentation rules apply; the full Local File is generally required for larger groups, including groups with net turnover of at least €45 million. Master File obligations generally apply to groups meeting the applicable €45 million net-turnover threshold. These thresholds do not eliminate the arm's-length requirement or all reporting obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish tax law nevertheless applies residence, permanent-establishment, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, controlled-foreign-company, and transfer-pricing rules. A Spanish SL must support its functions, assets, risks, personnel, decision-making, and commercial rationale with contemporaneous evidence, particularly for cross-border copper purchases, sales, financing, logistics, and service arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable sales, falsifying invoices or inventory records, claiming fictitious expenses, or deliberately omitting taxable income or assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties depend on the conduct and tax shortfall and can be substantial. Tax fraud exceeding €120,000 per tax and tax period may constitute a criminal offence under the Spanish Criminal Code, generally punishable by one to five years' imprisonment and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding €600,000 or specified organised or offshore circumstances, may attract two to six years' imprisonment and a fine of two to six times the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability if they participate in or knowingly facilitate the offence, and may incur civil or tax liability under applicable statutory rules. Corporate limited liability does not shield an individual from personal criminal liability. Travel restrictions or other precautionary measures are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for related-party copper, financing, services, guarantees, or intellectual property; omitting required records or disclosures; or maintaining documentation inconsistent with actual conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust taxable income and assess additional tax and interest. Specific documentation and reporting breaches may attract fixed penalties, commonly calculated by data item and subject to statutory minimums, maximums, and caps; deliberate tax underpayment may additionally attract tax penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SL is ordinarily the taxpayer. Directors may be held liable under statutory subsidiary or joint-liability provisions where the legal requirements are met, including culpable participation, obstruction, or failure to discharge specified duties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to non-residents without withholding, or applying treaty or EU relief without adequate evidence or eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unwithheld tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Incorrect relief claims may be reversed, and treaty or EU benefits may be denied under anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SL is generally responsible for withholding and remittance. Directors may incur personal liability only under applicable statutory conditions, including culpable conduct or failure to meet legally assigned duties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT, customs, and copper-trade documentation fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using false suppliers or invoices, misdescribing origin or grade, misusing import VAT or customs procedures, or concealing beneficial ownership or shipment routes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include reassessed VAT or customs duties, interest, administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture where authorised, and criminal prosecution where conduct meets the relevant statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal or statutory liability may arise from knowing participation, instruction, or facilitation. Corporate status does not immunise directors from offences they commit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling proceeds of crime, disguising counterparties or beneficial owners, circumventing applicable financial sanctions, or knowingly processing prohibited transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML and sanctions consequences depend on the breach and may include substantial administrative fines, confiscation, activity restrictions, and criminal penalties for money laundering or related offences. Applicable EU sanctions and export-control measures must be assessed for each counterparty, origin, destination, and payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate may face personal criminal and administrative consequences. A travel ban is not an automatic sanction; precautionary restrictions require a legal basis and competent-authority action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of limited liability or sham-company structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling company and personal assets, using the SL to conceal unlawful activity, stripping assets to defeat creditors, or operating without genuine corporate records or governance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A court may disregard limited liability in exceptional cases where the legal requirements for abuse, fraud, or sham conduct are established; directors may also face insolvency, tax, civil, or criminal consequences under the applicable statutes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is exceptional and not automatic. Directors may be ordered to pay civil compensation or be held liable for company debts where statutory grounds are met; imprisonment or travel restrictions arise only where independently authorised by law and imposed by the competent court.
